expectations.text: Rejects the simultaneous multi-surface launch and sequences one new surface at a time within a stated capacity number
expectations.evidence: "It ships four new surfaces at once"; the proposed sequence is weeks 1-3, 3-9, 8-13 with a concurrency gate.

expectations.text: States the reason: several concurrent launches yield half-measured surfaces with no clean signal from any, plus a standing maintenance bill for all
expectations.evidence: "you couldn't tell afterwards which surface matters"; "five release pipelines, five idiom reviews and five support queues, for years".

expectations.text: Asks for or forces a sustained-capacity number: how many surfaces the team can build, document, support, and keep releasing for years
expectations.evidence: "How many surfaces can the team really sustain at once?"

expectations.text: Blocks the five-language SDK plan until the spec is a linted source of truth in CI, because SDKs derive from that contract
expectations.evidence: "No derived surface is scheduled before this"; the spec is moved into the repo and linted in CI.

expectations.text: Flags the hand-updated wiki OpenAPI file as spec drift to fix before any derived surface is scheduled
expectations.evidence: "The spec lives in a wiki and drifts"; "A hand-edited wiki page would force you to fix every SDK separately."

expectations.text: Cites the one-spec-propagates-everywhere pattern (major platforms generating SDKs, docs, and MCP from one OpenAPI source of truth)
expectations.evidence: "Stripe, Twilio and Cloudflare each generate them from one source of truth, so a single change propagates everywhere."

expectations.text: Defers or removes the GraphQL endpoint absent a named, integrator-confirmed pain
expectations.evidence: "GraphQL has no named pain... It earns a slot only when integrators confirm."

expectations.text: Moves per-client and per-surface usage telemetry instrumentation to an early plan item instead of after launch
expectations.evidence: "Telemetry must come first. The plan says 'analytics after the surfaces are live', which is backwards."

expectations.text: Keeps webhooks as the near-term addition riding the existing REST infrastructure
expectations.evidence: Webhooks are near-term (weeks 3-9), but the plan never says they ride the existing REST infrastructure.

expectations.text: Cites the capacity-matched precedent: SDK languages added only once tooling made supporting them sustainable, or the principle that two surfaces done properly beat six done badly
expectations.evidence: "Twilio added languages only once its tooling could support them sustainably"; "two surfaces done properly beat six done badly".

expectations.text: Assigns surviving surfaces reversal-cost tiers, including server SDKs as high because method signatures bake directly into customer code
expectations.evidence: "Server SDKs have a high reversal cost because their method signatures end up in customer code (Hyrum's Law)."
